title: Manual Cryogenic Pulverisation of Tissue for RNA Extractions
author: Ashleigh Porter

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Cut and weigh the tissue samples and record the specimen, weight, and tissue origin.

substeps.instruction: Cut a lentil sized piece of formalin-fixed, ethanol-preserved, or otherwise chemically preserved tissue.
Weigh the tissue and record the specimen, weight, and tissue origin (e.g., organ).

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Equipment
steps.instruction: Gather all necessary materials and prepare the digestion buffer tubes.

substeps.instruction: Bring liquid nitrogen, tissue tubes, biopulveriser, proteinase K, and 2 X buffer to the laboratory.
Prepare eppendorf tubes containing 20uL proteinase K and 200uL 2 X Buffer for the number of samples to be processed.

steps.title: Store and Maintain Tissue
steps.instruction: Ensure tissue remains submerged in preservative to prevent drying.

substeps.instruction: Store tissue in eppendorf tubes in the original preservative fluid (or 70% ethanol) so that it is fully submerged.

steps.title: Chill Biopulveriser
steps.instruction: Cool the biopulveriser using liquid nitrogen while using appropriate safety gear.

substeps.instruction: Pour ~0.5L of liquid nitrogen into a cryogenically safe transport container to use per 10 samples.
Pour liquid nitrogen into a cryogenically safe container (e.g., metal tray, 20 cm x 20 cm x 10 cm) to create a shallow layer.
Place biopulveriser into the liquid nitrogen for ~1 minute so that each part is bathed.
Use tongs and gloves to avoid cryogenic burns.

steps.title: Load Biopulveriser
steps.instruction: Assemble the biopulveriser and load the tissue sample.

substeps.instruction: Remove biopulveriser components and place on a clean bench; fit pieces 1 and 2 together.
Use clean fine forceps to place the lentil sized piece of tissue on the end of piece 3 (usually the rough edge).
Using a clean eppendorf, carefully load the biopulveriser container with ~0.5-1ml fresh liquid nitrogen.
Wait until the liquid nitrogen has 'dried off' in the container.

steps.title: Pulverise Tissue
steps.instruction: Remove preservatives and mechanically pulverise the tissue into dust.

substeps.instruction: Remove 70% ethanol or other preservative from the tissues using a pipette.
Place piece 3 into the biopulveriser.
Using the hammer, crush the tissue with one or two hard blows until it resembles dust.
Using a clean spatula, scrape the tissue dust into the pre-prepared eppendorf containing proteinase K and 2 x buffer.

steps.title: Process Multiple Samples
steps.instruction: Repeat the pulverisation process for all remaining samples.

substeps.instruction: Clean tweezers, spatula, and biopulveriser parts between uses with bleach, water, and ethanol.

steps.title: Digest Tissue
steps.instruction: Incubate the pulverised tissue in a shaker to ensure full digestion.

substeps.instruction: Place eppendorf tubes containing pulverised tissue, proteinase K, and 2 x Buffer into a pre-heated shaker at 65 °C for 2 hours.
If tissue is not fully digested after 2 hours, leave for up to 4 hours.

steps.title: Extract RNA
steps.instruction: Perform RNA extraction using the Zymo Quick-RNA Mini Prep kit.

substeps.instruction: Follow manufacturer's instructions, including DNaseI treatment.
Use a 40uL elution at the final step to increase RNA yield.
